stops.note: Italian soldiers' cry 'all'arme!', to arms!, gave the word
to arms!, a battle cry warning of attack, from arma
carried into French for a warning call or signal of danger
stops.meaning: a warning call or signal of danger

stops.note: first recorded around 1400 in the poet William Langland, still as the battle cry 'to arms!'
stops.meaning: a warning signal of danger, or a feeling of fear

current_meaning: a warning sound or signal of danger, or a feeling of fear or anxiety
